data.name: Gyanendra
data.long_meaning:
The name Gyanendra is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Gyan’ meaning knowledge and ‘Indra’ meaning sovereign or king.
Gyanendra is a name that signifies wisdom and power, a wise ruler who governs with knowledge and understanding.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gyanendra embodies the ancient Indian philosophical tradition that places great emphasis on the attainment of knowledge and wisdom as a means for individual growth and enlightenment. In Indian culture, the search for knowledge and wisdom is seen as a lifelong pursuit and a noble endeavor. Naming a child Gyanendra reflects the desire for that child to embody the qualities of a wise and enlightened leader, both in personal and professional spheres.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the gods and goddesses are believed to be enlightened beings, possessing vast amounts of wisdom and knowledge. The name Gyanendra, then, can be seen as a reminder of the ultimate goal of human existence - to strive towards the attainment of the divine wisdom and knowledge that will lead to liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The name serves as a daily reminder for the bearer to constantly seek knowledge and wisdom, and in doing so, align themselves closer to the divine.
